title: cargo_build_dirs requires a third array fullcycle never reads, held off by a lint disable
body:
## Problem

`cargo_build_dirs` (lib/helpers:1337) fills three arrays by name reference, and fullcycle, one of its two callers, never reads the third, which is why b4eed88 put a SC2034 disable at lib/cmd/fullcycle:1332 during the 0.1.8 cut. Called with two names, the function dies on "$3: unbound variable" (helpers:1338). Parked at the 0.1.8 cut; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Fix

The third array is optional: with no third name the function fills a local it discards. fullcycle drops `cargo_roots` and the disable. Measured in a clone: `bash -n` and `shellcheck -x` pass on helpers, fullcycle and check, and the two-, three- and four-name forms and an empty third name all behave.

## Done when

1. Called with two names, it fills both arrays and does not die; red at 2ce9411.
2. No SC2034 disable is left for it in lib/cmd/fullcycle.

## Resolution

Fixed at ce72a4ff. `cargo_build_dirs <crates> <trees> [<roots> [<configs>]]` takes its roots array as optional. Named as nothing, or as an empty name, the roots fill a local of the call's own, which is dropped when it returns. fullcycle judges trees and never roots, so it names two arrays, and `cargo_roots` and the SC2034 disable that held it are gone from lib/cmd/fullcycle. check targetdir, the other caller, names all four as before.

Two arms in fullcycle.bats call the function in both shapes: with two names, and with an empty third name and a configs array. The first builds a real crate whose config moves its tree, so it needs cargo; each call must return 0 with nothing on stderr, and between them they must name the crate, the tree cargo names and the config. The second has no crate, so cargo is never asked, and it holds both shapes on a runner without cargo: each call must return 0 with empty arrays and nothing on stderr. In both arms the dropped local's name must find no variable after each call, so roots that leak into a global are red, and a fixture that failed reports its own status.

Driven red on f5334fa1: two names died with "$3: unbound variable", and an empty third name had bash print "not a valid identifier" while the call ran on. The arm with no crate is red there with cargo off PATH. Three mutants each turn both arms red: requiring the third name again, passing an empty name to `local -n`, and deleting the local, which leaves the roots in a global. Either call's check alone catches the third, and with cargo off PATH the arm with no crate kills all three.

Declared limit: the check names the local, `_cbds_noroots`, so renaming the local means changing both arms with it.

The full suite on the landing tree, main with 0173 landed and this patch with 0166 v2, which shares lib/helpers and fullcycle.bats with it and landed just after it at b3f37f92: 2070 of 2070 ok and 0 not ok (seal 20261005-1225, .errors empty), every landed blob equal to the suited tree's.
